Petitioner is before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.57631 of 2019 which arose out of Crime No.108 of 2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 323 of the IPC.

2. Heard Sri S Mahesh, learned counsel appearing for petitioner, Sri Mahesh Shetty, learned High Court Government NC: 2023:KHC:21328 Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri Satyanarayana S Chalke, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3. The 2nd respondent is the complainant.
The petitioner is the accused.
The petitioner and the 2nd respondent get married in the year 2011 when they were at ages 55 and 50.

Alleging that the petitioner has meted out certain torture against the complainant, a complaint comes to be registered against the petitioner on 09.04.2019 and the complaint becomes a crime in, Crime No.108 of 2019 for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 323 of the IPC.
The police after investigation file a charge sheet.
The filing of the charge sheet, is what drives the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

4. Learned counsel Sri S Mahesh appearing for the petitioner would contend that the complaint or the charge sheet nowhere narrates any ingredient of offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 or 323 of the IPC and seeks quashment of the entire proceedings, as according to the learned counsel NC: 2023:KHC:21328 what the complainant has alleged is only a grievance and cannot form an allegation against her husband.

6. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and have perused the material on record.
7. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
The issue lies in a narrow compass, as the petitioner and the respondent have been a couple since 2011 having married at the age of 55 and 50 years.
After about 8 years of living together, the issue crops up on a particular day when the petitioner is said to have NC: 2023:KHC:21328 assaulted the complainant, which results in a complaint.

The complaint reads as follows:
"I have been married to T.P.Vasanth for more than 8 years we got married in 2011.

In the last three years since 2016 my husband T.P.Vasanth has been behaving very unpredictably losing his temper threatening me using foul language for very pretty matter he has even abused and shouted at his aged parents.

Just three months ago,
my husband even hit a metal ealker on my 97 years old father in law's leg.
On Wednesday 27th March, my husband got angry that no one had kept a bottle of water next to the bed when we were going to sleep.
He started abusing using foul language not wanting provoke him I said nothing and just lay down to sleep my husband also lay down.
Then he put his hand on me I just said please just go to sleep.

Suddenly my husband pulled me up roughly and grabbed me around the neck from behind, he started to choke me shouting 'now what will you do ! where will you run'.
I kept struggling to free myself suddenly he threw me off the bed and I flow across landing hard on the floor and skidding against the bathroom door.

He jumped off the bed still shouting abuses and again pulled me up and threw me down then he tried to open the cupboard where he keeps his gun but then remembered he had surrendered it because of the elections.
He turned back to grab me and I hit out and ran out of the room shouting for help calling my cook to come.

My husband ran after me and caught up with me in living room and flung me onto the wooden centre table he caught my hair and that was when my cook came running into the room and screamed "Bhaiya kya kar rahe ho!".

On a perusal of the complaint and summary of the charge sheet what would unmistakably emerge is,
absence of any ingredient of the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC.

Section 498A of the IPC reads as follows:
"498A Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty;-

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- Sri T.P. Vasanth vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118602303/
4 (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."

sentences.text: Cruelty as defined under Section 498A of the IPC should be for the purpose of demand of dowry.
The entire complaint or the charge sheet so filed by the police would not indicate any offence by the petitioner on that score.
Therefore, the offence NC: 2023:KHC:21328 under Section 498A of the IPC is loosely laid against the petitioner.
The offence, therefore, cannot be permitted to be continued against the petitioner.
8. Insofar as the offences punishable under Sections 504 and 323 of the IPC are concerned, the complaint clearly makes out ingredients of those offences, so does the charge sheet (supra).
Therefore, quashment of proceedings insofar as it concerns offence under Sections 504 and 323 of the IPC is not warranted.
It is for the petitioner to come out clean in the trial for those offences.

For the aforesaid offences, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is allowed in part.
(ii) The charge sheet in C.C.No.57631 of 2019 insofar as it concerns offence punishable under Sections 498A stands quashed.
NC: 2023:KHC:21328 (iii) The charge laid for the offence punishable under Sections 323 and 504 stands sustained.
